extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers applying for ERC Starting Grants (prospective Principal Investigators) and their Host Institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/evaluation criteria for submitting an ERC Starting Grant proposal: who may apply, host institution requirements, funding limits, submission procedure and how proposals are evaluated. Targeted at early-career researchers preparing a Starting Grant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — years since PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers of any nationality with 2-7 years of experience since completion of PhD (Extensions are possible under certain circumstances — see the latest ERC Work Programme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions to the 2-7 year window may be available under specified circumstances; consult the latest ERC Work Programme for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific track record and readiness for independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Talented early-career scientist who has already produced excellent supervised work, is ready to work independently and shows potential to be a research leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate a scientific track record showing great promise alongside an excellent research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal quality (excellence of project)
rubrics_metrics.description: An excellent research proposal that defines a high-quality, original research project; applications can be made in any field of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ERC operates a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities — choose the strongest, novel research case in any field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence as the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who evaluate proposals on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion; it is applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excellence covers both the quality of the research and the PI's profile. Peer reviewers assess and score; those meeting the quality threshold are ranked and funding is awarded according to ranking and available budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution — eligibility and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (Host Institution/HI). Grants are awarded to the Host Institution with the explicit commitment that this institution offers appropriate conditions for the Principal Investigator to independently direct the research and manage its funding for the duration of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any type of legal entity (universities, research centres, undertakings) can be a host, but legally must be based in an EU Member State or an Associated Country. The PI need not already work at the HI at submission but a mutual agreement and the host’s commitment are necessary if successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Principal Investigator requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant must be submitted by a single Principal Investigator (PI) in conjunction with and on behalf of their Host Institution (the applicant legal entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ERC funds projects led by one PI who is responsible for the project; team members are employed by the PI/host as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and international participation
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members; it is possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancies can be advertised on Euraxess-Jobs. 'Implementing Arrangements' exist to enable ERC-funded teams in Europe to host non-European talented scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of research — bottom-up approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research; the ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no thematic priorities: proposals are judged on scientific excellence irrespective of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial award limits and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grants may be awarded up to €1.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for shorter projects). An additional €1 million can be made available for eligible 'start-up' costs (researchers moving from a third country), major equipment, access to large facilities, or other major experimental/field work costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and mandatory documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents, and be submitted by the specified closing date in response to a Call for Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls are published on the ERC page, the European Commission’s Funding and Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal. Ensure all administrative forms, proposal sections and supplementary docs are present before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be submitted via the EU submission service. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by submitting a new version which overwrites the old one. Deadlines cannot be changed under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise yourself with the EU submission service and supporting online manuals. You will receive an acknowledgement of receipt for each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation structure — panels and remote referees
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 25 panels, each covering a sub-section of one of three domains (Social Sciences & Humanities; Life Sciences; Physical & Engineering Sciences). Each ERC panel consists of a chairman and 10-16 members selected by the ERC Scientific Council. Evaluation also relies on input from remote experts external to the panel (referees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chairs' names are published before the deadline; Panel Members' names are published after the evaluation is concluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring, quality threshold and budgetary cut-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess and score the proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the ranking-and-cutoff process is critical: meeting the quality threshold does not guarantee funding if budgetary cut-offs exclude lower-ranked but eligible proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation steps and recommended support
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call: find which ERC grant and which call is suitable, identify the host institution and team members, and contact the National Contact Point (NCP) for support. Once the call is open: read the call documents carefully, contact the host institution and gather all details needed for the application, start writing early and allow others to review your draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPs, peers and other scientists can provide useful feedback. Use online partner search services and the EU submission service guides and manuals.
